person.name: Mohamed Zaitoun
person.headline: Product engineering for merchant operations
person.intro: I manage merchant accounts and build tools for the reps and operations teams who support them.
about: People call me Zaitounish, a play on my surname and the word for olive. Before I managed merchant accounts, I sold online ordering and loyalty software to restaurant operators. Those conversations still shape the tools I build.

At Concentrix, I manage merchant accounts for DoorDash. I also lead the technical work on Merchant Success Hub. Earlier, I built language model applications at Augmentoria and studied data analysis through Udacity.

bullets: Manage a rotating portfolio of 400+ DoorDash merchant accounts, resolve operational issues and review progress against monthly and quarterly targets.
Built MSM Markup Tracker to replace manual pricing compliance reports. Markup sales grew 27% quarter over quarter and reached 133% of the quarterly target.
Built MSM Campaign Dispatcher to prepare tailored merchant campaigns in under 10 minutes. The tool contributed to a 17.9% increase in Concentrix vendor sales.
Reached 118% of sales quota selling online ordering, branded mobile apps and loyalty programs to restaurant operators.
Helped operators choose a setup for their business, from the first conversation through the close. Deal velocity improved by 20%.
Developed ArtifyAI v1.1, a text-to-image application. Fine-tuned Stable Diffusion on 5,000+ COCO images and integrated T5 to handle prompts in four languages.
Used MLflow and Hugging Face for experiment tracking and model versioning during a 177-hour AI and machine learning program.
Built and deployed 3+ language model applications with Python and LangChain for business tasks including data extraction and classification.
Built Gradio interfaces so colleagues could run the applications themselves and give feedback on the results.
Resolved 94% of technical issues on the first call across 1,000+ customer interactions. Maintained a 96% customer satisfaction rating.
Used Salesforce, VMware and Avaya to troubleshoot customer issues and record the resolution.

projects.name: Merchant Success Hub
projects.resumeDescription: Led technical delivery of a multi-tenant sales operations platform for three lines of business in Concentrix’s DoorDash program. Built React portfolio views and used Azure Functions and PostgreSQL row-level security to scope access by role and assignment. Account management’s weekly report preserves sales credit through team transfers and compares validated claims with official sales.
projects.summary: I led technical delivery of a sales platform for three DoorDash merchant teams at Concentrix, drawing on my own work as an account manager. Reps can turn a portfolio into a targeted campaign without rebuilding a merchant list. Managers can see where outreach is falling behind and redirect their team before month-end.
details: Built portfolio filtering and saved views on a shared platform for account management, early merchant support and retention.
Account management’s weekly report compares validated sales claims with official results and uses historical assignments to attribute credit.

case.contribution: Account management, early merchant support and retention each use the Hub differently. A missing menu photo gives a rep a reason to reach out to a new restaurant. For a retention rep, success means helping an inactive store take orders again. Both teams keep ownership of their work, even when they support the same merchant.

spotlight.title: Where should a sales lead step in?
paragraphs: Halfway through the month, two reps can be equally far from target for different reasons. One still has eligible stores that haven’t been approached. The other has submitted wins that are waiting for review.

The Hub gives the lead enough context to act. They can help the first rep choose merchants for outreach and get the second rep’s claims in front of a reviewer while there’s still time to influence the month.

story.title: From a merchant list to a sales opportunity
paragraphs: Portfolios and targets lived in spreadsheets, campaign preparation happened in a separate tool, and weekly reviews meant reconciling what reps submitted with official sales figures. I built the Hub’s portfolio views around the question I faced as an account manager. Which merchant has a reason to hear from me today?

An account manager can filter for promotion eligibility and prepare personalized outreach for the stores they select. Early merchant support uses menu and promotion data to find gaps at new restaurants. Retention reps follow inactive stores through reactivation. The teams share a platform, and each has a clear definition of a win.

story.title: One store, different owners
paragraphs: A restaurant can have several stores. The same store can have both an account manager and a retention rep. We designed the Hub’s multi-tenant data model around that reality. Each line of business owns its assignments. When a portfolio changes hands, dated assignments preserve who was responsible for each store before and after the transfer.

I built the portfolio filters and saved views in React so reps could keep the spreadsheet workflow they knew. Azure Functions and PostgreSQL enforce access by role, team and assignment. That gives a lead a view across their team’s accounts while each rep works their own portfolio.

story.title: Managing the sales floor before month-end
paragraphs: Team leads can see whether each rep is on pace for the month, which stores still need outreach and who is on shift to cover them. That gives a lead a practical choice during the week. They can coach a rep on their next promotion or move coverage to an overlooked group of merchants.

The sales claims pilot also distinguishes work awaiting review from approved wins. For pricing work, the Hub tracks whether a merchant’s lower menu markup held for 30 days. That gives a lead a basis for coaching on the outcome of the offer as well as the initial sale.

story.title: Sales figures leadership can explain
paragraphs: For the weekly account management review, business intelligence analysts can compare validated wins with official sales and narrow a difference to a team or product. Reporting leads publish the current week’s figures straight to the Google Sheets workbook leadership already uses. That removes the step of copying totals by hand.

We also separated who owns an account today from who earned a sale. If a rep moves teams on Friday, Tuesday’s sale still counts for the team that earned it. Managers can move people where merchants need them and still give a fair account of each team’s performance.

The tool contributed to a 17.9% increase in Concentrix vendor sales.

projects.name: ArtifyAI v1.1
projects.summary: A text-to-image application for prompts in English, German, Romanian and French.
details: Fine-tuned Stable Diffusion on 5,000+ COCO images and integrated T5 for multilingual prompts.

projects.name: Analyze A/B Test Results
projects.summary: Tested whether a new ecommerce landing page increased conversions using hypothesis testing and regression.
details: Compared conversion rates for the original and updated pages in a Jupyter notebook.

projects.name: Train RAG SemanticSearch
projects.summary: A notebook that breaks a machine learning text into passages and retrieves relevant passages by similarity.
details: Created embeddings for the passages and indexed them in Chroma for search with LangChain.

projects.name: Hypothetical Document Embeddings
projects.summary: A notebook exploring how a generated example answer can help retrieve relevant passages from hotel reviews.
details: Used LangChain to generate a hypothetical answer and embed it as a search query.

projects.name: US Census Demographic Data
projects.summary: Built two Tableau dashboards and a visual story from 2015 US county data to explore population, poverty and transportation.
details: Documented the design decisions behind each view and compared poverty with unemployment across counties.

projects.name: No Show Appointments
projects.summary: Explored more than 100,000 medical appointments in Brazil to identify patterns in attendance.
details: Used pandas and Matplotlib to examine appointment histories and characteristics associated with missed visits.

projects.name: Explore US Bikeshare Data
projects.summary: Compared trip duration, popular stations and travel times across Chicago, New York City and Washington, DC.
details: Wrote a Python program to calculate descriptive statistics from each city's bike share records.

projects.name: Query a Digital Music Store
projects.summary: Used SQL to answer four business questions about a digital music store, its customers and its invoices.
details: Queried a relational music store database to examine media sales and purchasing behavior.
